What we know—and what we need to confirm

The current public website presents programs, research, media and events, with member login linking to a separate experience. Your September feedback asks for independent editing, a move away from WordPress, an owned member portal and connected research properties. The supplied CMS diagnostic identifies content mixed with design controls. The August estate review supplies historical context. CMS fit, current inventory, portal parity and CRM permissions still require validation; this is not a completed infrastructure audit.

    The technical boundaries

    CMS content feeds public pages. Public forms and the portal call Django services. Django enforces identity and access, owns application data and connects to the existing CRM. Restricted resources must never be exposed through public builds or shared caches. API contracts, portal rendering, database, identity provider, hosting and CRM sync direction need validation with the backend owner.

      WHAT THIS STAGE MAKES POSSIBLE

      What the 12-week target depends on

      This framework assumes prompt access, an agreed migration volume, a focused MVP, available backend capacity and regular stakeholder decisions. Integrations start during development; weeks 9–12 cover end-to-end QA, final integration and launch. Backend estimates and milestones must be confirmed by the backend owner. Launch requires acceptance, permissions and migration verification, plus a tested rollback plan. Discovery may change the scope or sequence.

      The engine

      Sign-in & permissionsProtected resourcesData & APIsCRM integrationOperations & security
      Backend responsibilities

      Authentication, server authorization, data models, resource delivery, validation and CRM failure / retry handling, backend hosting, secrets, monitoring and backups. The backend team confirms its scope, effort, staffing and milestones.

      Out Leadership makes the business decisions. Content approvals, CMS editor feedback, CRM access and final acceptance. Frontend and backend validate the full journey together.

      Accessible by designKeyboard, contrast & clear states
      Fast by intentionSmall payloads, purposeful motion
      Ready for every screenMobile through desktop
      Secure where it countsServer-enforced member access
      Before we commit

      Confirm content and migration volume, ZoomForth exports and required parity, member roles / identity, HubSpot configuration and sandbox / API access, CMS workflows / licensing, domains, hosting, backend availability and review cadence. Storyblok remains a candidate until editors validate it.

      What is not priced or promised

      No project cost, vendor fee, fixed backend estimate or ranking guarantee is included. A new CRM, payments, advanced personalization, complex automation and additional portal parity require separate scope. The 12-week plan is a target, conditional on discovery and backend alignment.

      How we accept the release

      Verify priority content and redirects, editor publishing, member permissions, CRM submissions and failure handling, analytics, responsive / keyboard journeys, performance budget, training, backups and rollback. Target WCAG 2.2 AA and Core Web Vitals: LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1. These need implementation-stage measurement and are not certified results.
